question: is there a weight at which delivery becomes risky?

sources.title: Influence of maternal body mass index on pregnancy complications and outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis - PMC
The effect of methods used in the management of maternal obesity on pregnancy and birth outcomes: a systematic review with meta-analysis - PMC

text: Your doctor makes the medical call. There is **no single weight cutoff** where delivery suddenly becomes risky; estimated baby weight is imprecise, and ACOG notes that it is hard to predict birth weight accurately [1]. For suspected very large babies, induction at 37–40 weeks did **not clearly change cesarean or instrumental birth**, though it may reduce shoulder dystocia and fracture; the evidence is still limited for rare harms [1].

sources.title: Induction of labour at or near the end of pregnancy for babies suspected of being very large (macrosomia) | Cochrane

text: Your doctor makes the medical call. In simple words: there isn’t one exact baby weight where delivery suddenly becomes risky [1]. Bigger babies can raise the chance of labor problems, shoulder dystocia, and birth trauma, but weight estimates before birth are not very precise [1]. If a baby is thought to be very large, induction near the end of pregnancy has not clearly changed caesarean or instrumental birth rates; it may reduce fractures, but evidence is limited for rare harms like brachial plexus injury [2].
